summary.text: Sherm Packard (Sherman Packard on Ballotpedia) is a Republican member of the New Hampshire House of Representatives for Rockingham 16 who is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Ballotpedia says he was first elected to the House in 1990 and became House speaker after the death of Speaker Dick Hinch in December 2020.

paragraphs.text: Sherman Packard was born in 1949 in Manchester, New Hampshire, and is the son of Norman Packard, a Republican who previously served as president of the state Senate.

He worked for more than 30 years as a small business owner of an auto upholsterer, was a member of the New Hampshire Motorcyclists' Rights Organization, and served on the Rockingham County Executive Committee for 12 years.
Packard was elected to the New Hampshire House of Representatives in 1990 and held leadership positions including deputy Republican leader, House minority leader and speaker pro tempore.
He began serving as acting speaker upon the death of Speaker Dick Hinch on December 9, 2020, and was officially elected speaker on January 6, 2021.
For the 2023-2024 session, Ballotpedia lists him as chair of the Rules Committee.
